captions.text: GlarePilot: weather and sun glare where — and when — you’ll actually drive
Each place gets the forecast and sun position for the moment you reach it
Enter any US trip, or try a demo trip — demo trips use the live forecast for tomorrow
Albany → Boston, leaving 6:45 AM tomorrow — routing, then one batched forecast request
Trip summary (live data): drive 2h 49m, arrive 9:34 AM EDT, sun glare 35 min
Top recommendation: “ESE-bound sunrise glare 11 mi from Pittsfield, MA” — where, when, why and what to do
Sun glare map layer: the route is colored by glare severity when you pass each point
Scrub along the trip: forecast, sun height and your heading, minute by minute
Sun vs. heading: shaded wedge = windshield glare zone — here: Severe glare
Amherst → Chicago, leaving 8:00 AM tomorrow — a full day westbound into the sunset
Trip summary (live data): 14h 24m drive — arrival shown in Chicago time: 9:24 PM CDT
Map layers: Sun glare…
…Weather: forecast rain, snow, fog and wind at your arrival time…
…Daylight: day, low sun, twilight and night along the drive
Recommendation: “WSW-bound sunset glare 13 mi from Lorain, OH” — click to highlight it on the map and timeline
“When should I leave?” — same route, departures −3 h…+3 h, transparent exposure score
Lower bars = less glare, wet, wind and after-dark exposure; the best option is marked
Suggestion: “Leave 1 h earlier: Sun 7:00 AM EDT” → Try this departure
Re-evaluated instantly — after dark: 3h 14m → 2h 9m; arrive 8:24 PM CDT
Forecast checkpoints: local arrival time, weather and sun at each place on the route
Units: one click switches between °F · mi and °C · km
Phone layout (390 × 844): the same planner, stacked for small screens
Amherst → Chicago on a phone (live data): summary, map, timeline and advice
Free, keyless data: Open-Meteo forecasts · Valhalla/OSRM routing · SunCalc sun position Planning aid, not a safety system. Built with Kiro.
